newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia AT&T deal seen major breakthrough.
newsitem.headline: Nokia AT&T deal seen major breakthrough.

text.p: Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy said Thursday it signed a three-year contract worth $240 million to provide AT&T Wireless Services Inc. with wireless telephones.
The phones can be used on either analogue or next-generation digital networks, Nokia said.

"This new phone will allow our customers the flexibility to travel to all of our markets and utilize our various networks seamlessly," AT&T Wireless Executive Vice President Maggie Wilderotter said in a statement.

AT&T Corp. Wednesday introduced its new wireless service, which combines a phone, pager and personal messaging system in a single device that works across the country. The service is initially available in 40 major markets.
"(The deal) is a major breakthrough for Nokia," said Postipankki analyst Ilkka Salonen.
"It will be a good reference for Nokia and it may lead to more orders from other operators," Merita Bank analyst Martti Larjo said.
The three-year contract with AT&T's wireless services is the biggest single deal for Nokia's mobile phones arm in the United States and analysts said its value alone made it significant for Nokia.
AT&T Wireless will begin to deploy new PCS (Personal Communication Services) systems in 1997 and, when completed, its networks will cover about 80 percent of the U.S. population.

Nokia will supply AT&T Wireless with handsets with a default capability to switch to analogue networks when the phone is not operating in an AT&T Wireless digital network, thus giving users the flexibility to swap networks seamlessly.
Already strong before the announcement on the back of gains in the U.S. technology sector, Nokia shares extended gains after the contract was announced, hitting a nine-month high in Helsinki.
In New York, Nokia ADRs were up $2 at $47.50 on the New York Stock Exchange. AT&T's shares were down 50 cents at $38.875.
